objections.claim: The bounded card is not executable by a separate evaluator: change_surface lists only a config path (experiments/qwen_critic_effort_ab.json), measurement_ref is null, and no runner locator (path + sha256) is cited that (a) loads bench/weekly_upgrade_eval/fixtures.json, (b) invokes the wrapper per arm with the named profile, (c) extracts a critic decision, and (d) records per-call wall time. Without a pinned harness, arm execution and timing capture are not reproducible.
objections.falsifier: Cite a single existing runner path and sha256 in-repo whose entrypoint deterministically produces per-arm, per-fixture (decision, wall_time_ms) records from the specified profile and manifest; absent such a locator the card cannot be executed by an independent evaluator.

objections.claim: No grader is specified for critic_decision_accuracy. The four fixtures partition into fatal/proceed classes, but the proposal does not define how model output is parsed into a decision, what counts as 'malformed', or the ground-truth mapping per fixture. Two evaluators can therefore reach different accuracy tallies on identical outputs, violating deterministic pass adjudication.
objections.falsifier: Specify the exact decision-extraction rule (JSON field name / regex / schema id) and enumerate the ground-truth label for each of critic_fatal_circular, critic_fatal_dominance, critic_proceed_fixable, critic_proceed_theorem.

objections.claim: The >=10% median wall-time reduction claim is underpowered and confounded. With fixture_ids of size 4 and seeds=[0], each arm produces four paired timing samples on a shared vLLM Qwen server that co-resides with the Gemma server and uses --enable-prefix-caching; first-touch KV state, prefix-cache warmup, and cross-tenant load can each shift medians by >10% independently of reasoning_effort.
objections.falsifier: Require >=3 seeds or per-fixture repetitions with a warmup call per arm, interleaved arm order per fixture, and prefix-cache discipline (flush or paired warm state); if the >=10% median gap survives that protocol, wall-time confounding is ruled out.

objections.claim: The 'single delta' description understates the coupling. Switching Qwen reasoning_effort from xhigh to medium changes reasoning depth (and thus reasoning_chars), which affects both the target metric (wall time) and the observable that drives the accuracy metric (decision content). On n=4 the pass_rule cannot separate 'faster because less thinking' from 'faster because a cheaper policy is equally good'.
objections.falsifier: Record reasoning_chars per fixture per arm alongside wall_time and decision; if reasoning_chars are indistinguishable between arms the effort switch produced no work reduction and the wall-time gain is attributable to noise.

objections.claim: critic_decision_accuracy on four balanced items is coarsely quantized to {0.00,0.25,0.50,0.75,1.00}. 'candidate accuracy >= baseline accuracy' is trivially satisfied when both saturate and grossly punitive when a single item flips, and there is no stated confidence interval or per-item disagreement bound. This weakens the accuracy control in the pass_rule.
objections.falsifier: Either (a) broaden fixture_ids to include additional critic fixtures from the 12-fixture manifest to reduce quantization, or (b) tighten the accuracy rule to zero per-item decision disagreements between arms rather than an aggregate inequality.

cheapest_decisive_test: Before promotion, add a pinned runner locator (path + sha256) that reads bench/weekly_upgrade_eval/fixtures.json and emits per-arm (decision, reasoning_chars, wall_time_ms) records, plus a written decision-parse rule and ground-truth labels for the four fixtures; then rerun the paired trial with at least three seeds, a warmup call per arm, interleaved arm order, and identical prefix-cache state, and accept only if median wall time drops >=10% with zero per-item decision disagreements versus baseline.
residual_risks: Co-resident Gemma and Qwen vLLM servers with prefix caching enabled make paired wall-time medians on n=4 sensitive to first-touch cache warming and cross-tenant load, potentially producing >10% swings unrelated to reasoning_effort.
Single seed removes any variance estimate for Qwen's stochastic reasoning path; a favorable draw on four items can inflate both accuracy and speed comparisons.
Undefined decision grader can silently vary between evaluators, letting the same raw outputs pass or fail the accuracy condition.

Reducing critic effort from xhigh to medium may preserve accuracy on the balanced four-fixture subset while degrading on adjacent critic fixtures not evaluated, so a green pass does not generalize beyond the four items even if the local pass_rule fires.

Because 'candidate accuracy >= baseline' is quantized on n=4, a shared 3/4 result would pass while masking that both arms miss the same item; the run should not be read as evidence of decision preservation.
No cap on per-call latency; a candidate that median-wins but tail-loses could still increase p95/p99 latency in the critic path if later adopted.
